CXCVIII. Ego Johannes dictus Borowetz de Rowna, quia de licencia et permissione gratiosa serenissimi domini nostri regis Wencezlai 241 bona mea, que in dicta villa Rowna possideo, dare seu testari, cui voluero, possum, sicut suis litteris hoc mihi dignatus est confirmare, quarum quidem litterarum etiam tenor ob maioris certificacionis euidenciam per oitmia sequitur in hec verba: [Folgt die Urkunde N. CXCVII inserirt]. Idcirco ego ipse prefatus Johannes Borowetz de Rowna singulis ac vniuersis, tam qui pro nunc sunt, quam in posterum futuris, per hec infrascripta notum facio et recognosco publice ac manifeste, quod deliberato animo sanoque et maturo amicorum meorum consilio necnon heredum meorum, quorum quo- modolibet (?) interesse poterit, precipue tamen et expresse fratris Lamberti filii mei in Mylawsk ordinis Premonstratensis professi, Margharete quoque vxoris mee, sed et Agnesce ac Offzce ambarum liliurum mearum plenaria liberaque voluntate et consensu curiam ineam in prefata villa Rowna cum omnibus iuribus et iurisdictionibus ad eandem pertinentibus seu spectantibus, videlicet censibus et censnalibus agris pratis pascuis siluis rubetis cultis et inculfis riuis piscaciunibus omnibusque ac singulis terrenis vsufructibus, quocun- que soleant debeant uel possint nomine dici seu nuncupari, prout hactenus ego atque supradicti mei censuales ea cum omnibus suis pertinenciis usque in hanc diem habuimus tenuimus ac possedimus pacifice et quiete, honorabilibus et religiosis viris domino Stephaiio abbati et conuentui monasterii Sanete Corone ordinis Cystereiensis Praghensis dyocesis ex die presenti nunc (?) et deinceps temporibus perpetuis libere quiete ac pacifice tenendam habendam possidendam atque fruendam trado et condescendu deputo et assigno, ita ut nuK lus vmquam hominum, cuiuscunque status condicionis gradus siue sexus existat, pro supranominatis bonis uel qualicunque eorum parte prescriptos dominum abbatem, uel qui pro tempore fuerit, siue conuentum iuris quippiam nee potestatis habere possit uel debeat ammouendi impetendi molestandi neque etiam inferendi dampnum quodcuuque siue grauamen. Ad veriorem eciam confirmacionis cer tificacionis bona hac eadem tabulis terre inscribi eis feci et intabu- lari. Vt vero iamdicta huiusmodi mea tradicio condescensio deputacio assignacio et intabulaeio inconuulsa perpetuo et indistracta perma- nere nee cuiusquam hominis contradictione renisu uel obsistencia irritari quoquo modo possit aut infringi, supplicaui nobili et generoso domino domino Henrico de Rosenberg necnon strennuis et honestis viris domino Marchwardo militi de Poressyn, Pessykoni de Dudlyb Fontes. entries.english:
2 February 1406. Johann called Borowelz of Rowna gives his estate in the village of Rowna, with all its appurtenances, to Stephan, Abt and the convent of Goldenkron Monastery.

CXCVIII. I, Johann called Borowetz of Rowna, since our most serene lord König Wenceslaus has graciously granted me, by his permission and license, the right to give or bequeath my property in the said village of Rowna to whomever I wish, as he has deigned to confirm to me by his letters, whose full tenor follows in all respects for greater certainty [the charter CXCVII is inserted here], therefore I, the aforesaid Johann Borowetz of Rowna, make publicly and plainly known and acknowledge to all, both present and future, by what follows, that with deliberation, sound judgment and mature counsel of my friends and heirs whose interests may in any way be affected—especially and expressly my son Brother Lambert, professed in the Premonstratensian Order at Mylawsk, and with the full and free will and consent of my wife Margaret and both my daughters, Agnes and Offza—I now transfer, surrender, assign and grant to the honorable and religious men Lord Stephan, abbot, and the convent of the monastery of the Holy Crown of the Cistercian Order in the Prague diocese, to hold, have, possess and enjoy freely, quietly and peacefully from this day onward and for all time, my estate in the aforesaid village of Rowna, with all rights and jurisdiction belonging or pertaining to it: namely rents, rent-bearing lands, fields, meadows, pastures, woods, thickets, cultivated and uncultivated land, streams, fisheries, and every terrestrial usufruct, whatever name it may or ought to bear, just as I and the aforesaid rent-paying tenants have hitherto peacefully and quietly held, possessed and enjoyed it with all its appurtenances until this day. No person of any status, condition, rank or sex shall ever have or claim any right or power to remove or dispossess the aforesaid abbot, his successor, or the convent from the aforesaid property or any part of it, to bring any claim against them, molest them, or inflict any damage or grievance upon them. For more certain confirmation, I have also caused this property to be entered and registered for them in the land books. So that this my transfer, surrender, assignment, grant and registration may remain forever undisturbed and unimpaired, and may in no way be invalidated or broken by anyone’s opposition, resistance or contradiction, I asked the noble and distinguished Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg, and the valiant and honorable men Lord Marchward, knight of Poressyn, Pessyko of Dudlyb, and Myxiko of Myssnytz, my kinsmen, to attach their seals to this present letter, together with my own, as testimony to the foregoing; they willingly and graciously did so. We, Heinrich von Rosenberg, Marchward von Poressyn, Pessyko von Dudlyb and Myxiko von Myssnytz, also acknowledge and declare that, with full knowledge, good will and consent, we have caused our seals to be attached to this letter, together with the seal of the aforesaid Johann Borowetz, as testimony to the matters stated above. Given in the year of the Lord 1406, on the feast of the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

Five small seals hang from parchment tags. a) A shield bearing a goat; “S. Johannis de Bor.”, white wax. b) Red wax: shield with a rose, above it a helmet with the same crest; “S. Henrici de Roseberg”; compare CXLI. c) See CXCIV a; here in black wax. d) White wax, poorly impressed: a helmet with what may be a woman’s bust; [“S. Peskoni Dvdle …?”]. e) A helmet with the bust of a man wielding a sword; “S. Nicoli de Michnicz.”
